headline: Indian students protest after a medical exam leak

sources.title: India opposition leader Gandhi freed after detention at student-led protest
Thousands protest in India after clashes, despite Modi assuring action on exams
India's 'cockroach' protest continues after police crackdown | BBC News (video, BBC News)

chunks.text: More than 5,000 people [[gathered]] at Jantar Mantar, a protest site in Delhi, on Tuesday, July 22, [[a day after]] [[clashes]] {{broke out}} between police and marchers. The protest is over a national medical [[entrance exam]] whose papers [[leaked]] in May, forcing about two million [[candidates]] to take the test again. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Vadra were [[detained]] outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's [[residence]] and released that evening.

verbs.correct: To start suddenly, as fighting does
verbs.why: Break out means for something sudden and often violent to start, like fighting or a fire. Clashes broke out between police and protesters the day before this large gathering in Delhi.

chunks.text: The protests are organized by the Cockroach Janta Party, which {{grew out of}} an online joke two months ago and has since [[gained]] millions of followers. Led mainly by students, it wants Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to {{step down}}, the release of Sonam Wangchuk, an [[activist]] on [[hunger strike]] since June 28, and 10 million rupees, about $104,000, for each family of the [[dozen or so]] students who died.

verbs.wrong: To spend your childhood in a place
verbs.why: Grow out of means to develop naturally from something small or informal into something bigger. This protest movement grew out of a simple online joke just two months ago.

verbs.correct: To leave a position of authority
verbs.wrong: To get involved in order to help
verbs.why: Step down means to leave an important job or position, often under pressure. Protesters are demanding that the education minister step down over the exam leak scandal.

chunks.text: Monday's march toward parliament ended in violence, with police using [[tear gas]] and batons to {{hold back}} the [[crowd]]. Delhi Police said nearly 180 people were hurt, including 118 police and security staff and 60 [[protesters]]. The party's [[founder]], Abhijeet Dipke, said more than 150 protesters were in hospitals. Neither figure has been [[independently]] checked. Modi told [[lawmakers]] that his government acted [[as soon as]] it {{found out}} about the leak, that 13 people had been arrested, and that the re-test {{went ahead}} without problems.

verbs.correct: To stop someone from moving forward
verbs.why: Hold back means to physically stop people or a crowd from advancing. Police used tear gas and batons to hold back the crowd during Monday's march.

verbs.correct: To learn about something for the first time
verbs.wrong: To draw attention to an important fact
verbs.why: Find out means to learn a piece of information you did not know before. Modi said his government acted as soon as it found out about the exam leak.

verbs.wrong: To break a promise you made
verbs.why: Go ahead means that something continues to happen the way it was planned, without being stopped. Modi said the re-test went ahead without problems, despite the protests over the leak.

chunks.text: Pradhan said students [[deserve]] [[far better than]] being treated as [[props]] in a political [[campaign]]. Hundreds {{stayed on}} at Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, and smaller protests were held in Mumbai and Bengaluru. The re-test is finished, but the party says it will {{keep up}} its protests until the government {{brings in}} changes to the way exams are run.

verbs.correct: To remain in a place longer than expected
verbs.wrong: To go to bed much later than usual
verbs.why: Stay on means to remain somewhere after you might have been expected to leave. Hundreds of protesters stayed on at Jantar Mantar even after the main march had ended.

verbs.wrong: To deliberately avoid a certain place
verbs.why: Keep up means to continue an effort at the same steady pace, without stopping or losing energy. The party says it will keep up its protests until the government changes how exams are run.

verbs.correct: To introduce a new rule or change
verbs.wrong: To mention a subject in a discussion
verbs.why: Bring in means to introduce something new, especially a law, rule, or policy. Protesters want the government to bring in real changes to how exams are written and protected.

mainIdea.s: Thousands of students are protesting in Delhi after a medical exam leak forced a retest. The group behind the protests wants the education minister to resign and demands changes to exam rules.
mainIdea.why: The papers for the exam leaked in May, forcing about two million candidates to retake it. The party's central demand is that the education minister step down.

mainIdea.s: Protesters in Delhi are demanding that the prime minister resign over the exam leak scandal. They have also gathered for several days to demand payments for the families of students who died.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the education minister is the one asked to resign, not the prime minister, who only assured lawmakers the leak was handled.

mainIdea.s: University students in northern India went on strike this year over unpaid scholarship funds owed by the state. The protest ended after officials promised to release the money within a month.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a separate scholarship funding strike by university students, not the medical exam leak protests in Delhi.
